name: Both-Bone Forearm Fracture
definition: Fracture of both radius and ulna shafts, usually requiring restoration of length, alignment and forearm rotation.

investigations.principle: Forearm radiographs must include wrist and elbow.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, physeal, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Adult displaced both-bone fractures commonly require operative fixation.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Hasta-bhagna phenotype may be documented after modern stabilization.

patientEducation.summary: Fracture of both radius and ulna shafts, usually requiring restoration of length, alignment and forearm rotation.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, open injury, severe deformity, rapidly progressive neurological symptoms, suspected infection or other listed red flags.
